On input 0, the prose says to set (s,t)=(s+t, t+1) in the respective moduli. On input 1, it says to set (s,t)=(2s+t+1, s+t) in the respective moduli. The parenthetical requirement that both right-hand sides use the pre-input state means the two coordinates are updated simultaneously from the old (s,t), not sequentially. Thus for any state in Z4 x Z3 and any bit b in {0,1}, there is exactly one next state. This step only fixes the deterministic transition function; it does not yet use the input probabilities or count any strings.
